frontMatter.introduction:
Standard Operating Procedures (SOPs) are formally approved and documented instructions that define how routine and critical activities are performed within Padma Satel Arab Fashion Ltd. These procedures serve as a structured framework ensuring that all operations are carried out in a consistent, controlled, accountable, and compliant manner across the entire organization.

As a garments and apparel manufacturing company in Bangladesh supplying international markets, Padma Satel Arab Fashion Ltd. operates in a regulatory and business environment that demands adherence to labor laws, environmental standards, occupational safety requirements, ethical business conduct, and international sustainability frameworks. This SOP Manual reflects the Company's strong commitment to meeting and exceeding these expectations.

This SOP Manual has been developed to serve dual purposes: as a comprehensive internal operational guideline and as evidence of the Company's sustainability and compliance management systems for international buyer audits and sustainability assessments including BSCI, SMETA, WRAP, and similar programs.

This SOP Manual is designed to:
Standardize workflows, processes, and operational practices across all departments and production functions
Ensure adherence to quality, safety, environmental, labor rights, and ethical standards applicable to the RMG sector in Bangladesh
Promote transparency, accountability, and responsible decision-making at all organizational levels
Support employee training, capacity building, and knowledge continuity across all functions
Strengthen internal controls, governance mechanisms, and audit readiness
Demonstrate commitment to international sustainability frameworks including ISO 14001, ISO 45001, SA8000, and applicable buyer Codes of Conduct
Facilitate continuous improvement in environmental, social, and governance (ESG) performance

All employees and relevant stakeholders are expected to understand, follow, and uphold the procedures outlined in this manual. Compliance with SOPs is mandatory and forms an integral part of the Company's governance, quality management, and sustainability framework.
frontMatter.scope:
This Standard Operating Procedure (SOP) Manual is applicable to all operational, support, and administrative functions of Padma Satel Arab Fashions Ltd. (hereinafter referred to as “the Company”). It governs all activities carried out within the Company that directly or indirectly influence operational efficiency, product quality, regulatory compliance, worker welfare, environmental responsibility, and ethical business conduct.

The provisions of this SOP Manual apply to all individuals and entities engaged in or associated with the Company’s operations, including but not limited to:
All permanent, temporary, contractual, probationary, and casual employees working within the Company
Management, supervisory, technical, and administrative personnel at all levels of the organization
Trainees, apprentices, interns, and consultants engaged by the Company
Contractors, service providers, vendors, suppliers, and subcontractors performing activities within or on behalf of the Company

This SOP Manual is applicable across all operational areas and departments, including but not limited to production facilities, cutting, sewing, finishing, packing, maintenance and utility operations, warehouses, administrative offices, and worker welfare facilities within the Company premises.

All departments, including Production, Quality Assurance, Maintenance, Human Resources, Administration, Finance, Procurement, Compliance, Environment, Health & Safety (EHS), Sustainability, and Information Technology, are required to adhere to the relevant SOPs applicable to their functions and responsibilities.

Every individual performing tasks on behalf of the Company is required to follow the procedures outlined in this SOP Manual in accordance with their assigned roles. Any deviation or non-compliance shall be addressed through corrective and disciplinary actions in line with the Company’s internal policies and management systems.

This SOP Manual shall remain in effect unless formally revised, updated, or withdrawn through the Company’s approved document control and revision process.
frontMatter.reviewMechanism:
Governance Principle
All Standard Operating Procedures within this manual are subject to a formal review and control framework ensuring their continued accuracy, legal compliance, operational relevance, and alignment with the Company's sustainability commitments. Padma Satel Arab Fashion Ltd. maintains a disciplined document management culture where procedures are regularly reviewed, updated as required, approved by appropriate authority, and communicated effectively to all affected personnel across all departments.

Review Cycle Framework
Annual Scheduled Review: Comprehensive content evaluation against current practices and regulations (Department Head)
Regulatory / Legal Change: Immediate compliance update to align with new requirements (Compliance / Legal)
Process or Technology Change: Operational alignment revision for changed process (Concerned Department)
Audit Observation or Finding: Corrective revision to address identified gap (Quality / Compliance)
Incident or Near Miss: Risk-based update to prevent recurrence (EHS / Risk Function)
Customer or Certification Requirement: Update to meet new or changed external requirement (Compliance / Management)
Management Directive: Strategic alignment update (Senior Management)

Review Process Stages
1. Stage 1 – Initiation: The SOP Owner initiates the review process before the defined review due date or immediately upon identification of a triggering event. The review date and scope are formally communicated to all contributing departments.
2. Stage 2 – Evaluation: SOP content is assessed against current regulatory requirements, internal audit findings, risk assessments, incident reports, operational performance data, and stakeholder feedback to determine whether revision is required.
3. Stage 3 – Revision: Where improvements or corrections are identified, changes are documented clearly. Version number is updated in the document control header, and revision history records the date, nature, and author of all changes made.
4. Stage 4 – Approval and Authorization: Revised SOPs are submitted for approval per the approval matrix. Department Head reviews and approves departmental content. Compliance function reviews for regulatory alignment. Top Management approves where strategic significance warrants senior approval.
5. Stage 5 – Communication and Training: Updated SOPs are communicated to all affected employees. Where changes affect operational practices, targeted awareness or training is conducted before the updated SOP takes operational effect.
6. Stage 6 – Distribution and Version Control: Updated SOPs are distributed to all relevant departments with the new version number and effective date. Previous versions are withdrawn from active use, clearly marked as superseded, and archived in the document management system.
7. Stage 7 – Archival Control: Superseded versions are archived securely for the retention period specified in the Document Retention Policy, clearly marked 'Superseded – Not for Current Use', and cannot be retrieved for operational use.

Oversight and Continuous Governance
Senior Management reviews the overall SOP governance system during quarterly Management Review Meetings to ensure alignment with business objectives, compliance requirements, buyer assessment commitments, and risk management priorities. SOP compliance is assessed during annual internal audits. Systemic gaps identified trigger corrective and preventive actions at the organizational level. SOP performance indicators including audit findings, training completion rates, and non-conformance trends are reported to management at each review cycle.

sops.title: FAIR EMPLOYMENT, WORKER RIGHTS & LABOR STANDARDS

blocks.text: The purpose of this SOP is to establish a systematic approach for efficient energy management and greenhouse gas (GHG) emission reduction at Padma Satel Arab Fashions Ltd.. This SOP aims to improve energy efficiency, optimize resource utilization, monitor and reduce GHG emissions, ensure compliance with applicable legal and international requirements, and support the company’s sustainability and environmental commitments.

This SOP applies to all permanent, temporary, contractual, and casual workers engaged at Padma Satel Arab Fashion Ltd.'s production facilities, warehouses, and administrative areas. It covers all phases of the employment relationship from recruitment through separation.

rows.definition: Any individual directly employed or engaged by the Company to perform production, utility, or support activities.
The total hours worked per day or per week including regular and any overtime hours.
Any concern, complaint, or dissatisfaction raised by a worker regarding their employment or workplace conditions.
The right of workers to organize, join, or form worker representative bodies without interference.
The legally mandated minimum compensation as determined by the Bangladesh Wage Board for the RMG sector.

responsibilities: Manages recruitment, onboarding, employment contracts, payroll, leave management, and labor law compliance
Monitors labor practice adherence, conducts internal audits, manages corrective actions, maintains compliance records
Implement fair treatment on the floor, monitor working hours, ensure worker welfare, report issues to HR
Facilitates structured dialogue between workers and management on working conditions and welfare
Follow Company policies, participate in surveys, and report violations through grievance channels

substeps.text: All workers are recruited based on merit, skill, and operational requirements without discrimination on grounds of gender, religion, ethnicity, age, disability, marital status, or political affiliation.

Written employment contracts are provided to all workers in Bengali (Bangla) language before commencement of employment, clearly stating job role, wages, working hours, leave entitlements, and terms of separation.

Employment of children below the minimum legal working age as defined under Bangladesh Labour Act is strictly prohibited. Age verification documents including National ID or birth certificate are collected during recruitment.
Workers are not required to deposit identity documents, passports, or any personal documents as a condition of employment.
No recruitment fees or related costs are charged to workers. All costs associated with recruitment are borne solely by the Company.
A formal induction program is conducted for all new employees before commencing independent work, covering Company policies, safety procedures, worker rights, and job-specific work instructions.
Employment of workers through forced, bonded, compulsory, or trafficked labor is strictly prohibited in all circumstances.
Regular working hours do not exceed 8 hours per day and 48 hours per week in compliance with Bangladesh Labour Act.
Overtime is strictly voluntary, compensated at the legally required premium rate (minimum 200% of regular wage), and does not exceed permissible limits under applicable law.
Workers receive at least one full rest day per week. Adequate rest breaks are provided during working shifts in compliance with legal requirements.
Working hour records including attendance registers, overtime logs, and shift records are maintained accurately in the HR management system and are always available for inspection.
During peak production periods, overtime requirements are communicated in advance. Worker consent is obtained and documented prior to any overtime scheduling beyond standard hours.
Workers are not penalized, threatened, or subjected to adverse treatment for declining overtime beyond legally permissible limits.
All workers receive wages equal to or exceeding the minimum wage determined by the Bangladesh National Minimum Wage Board for the garment sector.
Wages are paid regularly and on time through a documented payroll system. Individual pay slips are provided to all workers clearly showing gross earnings, deductions, and net pay.
Unlawful or unauthorized deductions from wages are strictly prohibited. Any permissible deductions are transparently communicated to workers before commencement of employment.

Workers receive all legally mandated benefits including annual festival bonuses (Eid-ul-Fitr and Eid-ul-Adha), earned annual leave, casual leave, sick leave, maternity leave, and provident fund contributions as applicable.
Production incentives and attendance bonuses are paid according to documented Company policies communicated to workers.
Wages and benefit structures are reviewed periodically to ensure continued compliance with legal revisions and market competitiveness.

steps.heading: 1.4 Freedom of Association and Worker Representation

substeps.text: Workers have the right to form, join, or participate in worker representative bodies, trade unions, or participation committees as permitted under Bangladesh Labour Act without interference, coercion, or retaliation.

A Worker Participation Committee (WPC) is established and actively operational at the factory, facilitating regular structured dialogue between management and workers on matters related to production, welfare, wages, and working conditions.
WPC meetings are conducted at regular intervals (minimum quarterly). Meeting agendas, attendance records, minutes, and follow-up action records are maintained by HR.
Workers participating in union or WPC activities are fully protected from retaliation, discrimination, demotion, or adverse employment actions.
Management engages constructively with WPC representatives on improvements to wages, working conditions, safety practices, and worker welfare facilities.
All forms of physical, verbal, psychological, or sexual harassment in the workplace are strictly prohibited and subject to serious disciplinary action including immediate dismissal where warranted.
A formal Anti-Harassment and Non-Discrimination Policy are documented, signed by Top Management, and communicated to all employees during induction training and periodic refresher programs.
A dedicated Anti-Harassment Committee with trained members from multiple departments is established to receive, investigate, and resolve harassment complaints confidentially.
Workers are encouraged to report harassment, abuse, or discrimination through safe, confidential reporting channels without fear of retaliation or adverse treatment.
The Company does not discriminate in hiring, promotion, training, transfer, or termination based on gender, religion, ethnicity, age, disability, pregnancy status, or political affiliation.

Multiple grievance channels are maintained including a physical suggestion and complaint box, direct reporting to supervisors and HR, a dedicated floor-level complaints register, and a confidential anonymous reporting option.
All grievances received are logged, acknowledged to the worker within 3 working days, investigated objectively, and resolved within defined timelines not exceeding 15 working days for standard cases.
Workers raising genuine grievances are fully protected from any retaliation, adverse treatment, or unfair employment actions arising from the grievance submission.
Grievance records including nature of complaint, investigation steps, resolution action, and worker feedback are maintained for minimum 3 years for monitoring and audit purposes.
The grievance mechanism is communicated to all workers through Bengali-language notice boards, induction training, WPC meetings, and periodic floor-level awareness sessions.
Clean and safe drinking water is available at accessible locations throughout the facility including production floors, canteen areas, and common spaces.
Separate and adequate toilet and washroom facilities are maintained for male and female workers in sufficient numbers as per applicable legal standards.
A clean and hygienic canteen or dining area with affordable or subsidized meals is provided and maintained throughout operational hours.
A fully equipped first aid room with trained first aid personnel and adequate medical supplies is operational during all working shifts.
Designated prayer spaces (Namaz rooms) are provided within the facility for workers to observe religious practices.
Crèche or childcare facilities are provided for female workers with young children in compliance with Bangladesh Labour Act requirements.
Adequate lighting, ventilation, and temperature management systems are maintained across production areas to ensure worker comfort and health.

steps.heading: 1.8 Employee Satisfaction and Worker Voice Programs

substeps.text: Annual Employee Satisfaction Surveys are conducted covering working conditions, management practices, safety, compensation, leave, welfare facilities, and overall workplace environment.
Survey results are analyzed by HR and management, and improvement action plans are developed and communicated to workers through WPC meetings and notice board postings.
Third-party worker voice surveys may be conducted by customers or certification bodies to independently verify worker welfare conditions.
Worker feedback from surveys, WPC meetings, and grievance mechanisms is reviewed by management and formally recorded with associated action plans.

blocks.text: All labor practices comply with the Bangladesh Labour Act, Export Processing Zones Authority (EPZA) regulations where applicable, ILO Core Conventions, and applicable buyer Codes of Conduct. Records of employment contracts, payroll registers, working time logs, WPC minutes, grievance records, and welfare facility inspection reports are maintained for a minimum of 5 years and are made available during internal and external audits upon request.

The Company plans to progressively strengthen labor management systems through digitization of payroll and attendance records, enhancement of worker voice mechanisms including mobile-accessible reporting tools, expansion of skills development programs for workers and supervisors, and participation in industry-level labor standards improvement initiatives applicable to the Bangladesh RMG sector.

narrative.text: Labor compliance performance indicators including overtime hours, grievance closure rates, WPC meeting frequency, wage compliance, and welfare facility inspection results are reviewed monthly by HR and reported to senior management quarterly. Annual internal labor audits are conducted by the Compliance team with findings tracked to resolution. Labor performance trends are included in management review meeting agendas.

sops.title: OCCUPATIONAL HEALTH, SAFETY & WORKPLACE ACCIDENT PREVENTION

blocks.text: Padma Satel Arab Fashion Ltd. is committed to providing a safe and healthy working environment for all employees, contractors, and visitors across all facility areas. The Company maintains a comprehensive Occupational Health and Safety (OHS) management system to systematically identify, assess, control, and eliminate workplace hazards and risks. Compliance with the Bangladesh Labour Act, Fire Prevention and Extinguishing Act, and applicable international safety standards including ISO 45001 forms the foundation of this commitment. Zero tolerance for preventable accidents is a core organizational value embedded across all operations.

This SOP applies to all production floors, cutting sections, sewing lines, finishing areas, utility rooms, warehouses, administrative offices, canteens, staircases, and all common areas within the Company's facility. It covers all activities including regular production, maintenance, cleaning, and emergency situations.

rows.definition: Any source, situation, or act with potential to cause harm, injury, or illness to workers.
A systematic process of identifying hazards, evaluating associated risks, and determining appropriate control measures.
Personal Protective Equipment worn to minimize exposure to identified workplace hazards.
Any unplanned event resulting in or with potential to result in injury, illness, property damage, or production loss.
An incident that did not result in harm but had the potential to do so under slightly different circumstances.
Lockout/Tagout procedure applied during equipment maintenance to prevent accidental energization.

responsibilities: report all incidents and near misses

blocks.text:
Comprehensive safety induction training is mandatory for all new employees before commencing work on the production floor covering fire safety, emergency evacuation, PPE usage, machine safety, chemical hazards, and first aid awareness.
Periodic refresher training on fire safety, emergency procedures, PPE usage, chemical handling, machine safety, and ergonomics is conducted for all workers minimum annually with attendance documented.
Safety awareness materials including posters, notices, warning signs, and visual work instructions in Bengali are displayed prominently throughout all facility areas.
Regular safety toolbox talks (minimum monthly) are conducted at department or line level addressing current safety concerns and reinforcing safe working practices.
Safety training attendance records, toolbox talk minutes, drill results, and awareness documentation are maintained for minimum 3 years for audit verification.

All occupational health and safety activities comply with the Bangladesh Labour Act, Fire Prevention and Extinguishing Act, Bangladesh National Building Code (BNBC) structural safety provisions, and applicable international standards. The Company maintains current fire safety certificates, structural compliance documentation, and all mandatory safety-related registrations and approvals. Safety compliance records including inspection reports, drill records, incident registers, and training documentation are retained for minimum 5 years and are made available upon request during internal and external audits.

The Company plans to strengthen its OHS management system through implementation of a digital incident reporting and tracking platform, expansion of health surveillance programs for high-risk occupational exposure groups, introduction of ergonomic improvement initiatives for sewing machine operators and cutting team members, and periodic third-party structural and electrical safety assessments. Enhanced safety leadership training for supervisors and line leaders is planned to embed safety accountability at every level of the production floor.

narrative.text: OHS performance indicators including Lost Time Injury Frequency Rate (LTIFR), Total Recordable Injury Rate (TRIR), near miss reporting frequency, PPE compliance rates, and fire drill completion records are reviewed monthly by the Safety Officer and reported to management quarterly. Annual OHS management reviews assess overall safety performance against set targets and determine priorities for the coming year. Corrective actions from audit findings and incident investigations are tracked to closure in the CAPA register.

sops.title: CLIMATE PHYSICAL RISK ASSESSMENT & BUSINESS RESILIENCE

blocks.text: Padma Satel Arab Fashion Ltd. operates in Bangladesh, which is among the most climate-vulnerable countries globally. Physical climate risks including river flooding, flash floods, tropical cyclones, storm surges, extreme heat events, and the long-term effects of sea-level rise pose real and increasing threats to production continuity, supply chain reliability, infrastructure integrity, and worker safety. This SOP establishes systematic procedures for identifying, assessing, managing, and responding to climate-related physical risks across all Company operations.

This SOP applies to all facility operations, infrastructure assets, supply chain activities, worker safety planning, and business continuity management processes in relation to climate physical risk exposure and emergency preparedness.

rows.definition: Risks arising from the physical effects of climate change including extreme weather events (acute risks) and longer-term climate shifts (chronic risks).
Short-term, event-driven climate risks such as cyclones, floods, and extreme heat events.
Longer-term shifts in climate conditions such as rising average temperatures, changing rainfall patterns, and sea-level rise.
A documented plan outlining procedures to maintain or restore business operations during and after a disruptive event.

responsibilities: Identify climate risks within their area

body.text: Bangladesh's low-lying geography and dense river network create significant seasonal flood exposure that can disrupt road access, affect material supply chains, and potentially affect ground-floor facility areas.

steps.heading: Tropical cyclones and associated storm surges

body.text: The Bay of Bengal generates periodic severe cyclones causing high winds, storm surge flooding, and infrastructure damage particularly in coastal and low-elevation areas.
Rising average temperatures and increasing frequency of extreme heat days in Bangladesh create heat stress risks for workers, especially in production areas with heat-generating machinery.
Changes in monsoon rainfall patterns affect transportation logistics, supplier delivery reliability, and drainage system performance.
Key raw material suppliers including fabric mills and accessory manufacturers may be affected by climate events causing material supply delays or shortages.

steps.heading: A formal climate risk assessment is conducted and documented

body.text: A formal climate risk assessment is conducted and documented identifying each risk's likelihood, potential operational impact severity, and current control measures in place.
Risk assessments evaluate potential impacts on production continuity, infrastructure integrity, worker health and safety, supply chain reliability, and financial performance.
High-priority climate risks are designated for priority mitigation and adaptation action planning with defined owners and implementation timelines.

steps.heading: Climate risk assessments are reviewed and updated annually

body.text: Climate risk assessments are reviewed and updated annually and whenever significant new climate information or operational changes require revision.

Flood protection measures including regular cleaning and maintenance of facility drainage systems, installation of flood barriers at ground-floor entry points where applicable, and elevation of critical electrical equipment above potential flood levels are implemented.

Heat stress management protocols are followed including provision of sufficient cool drinking water stations, mandatory rest breaks during extreme heat conditions, shade provisions in outdoor work areas, and HVAC system optimization.

Building infrastructure resilience is assessed against design standards for wind loading and precipitation. Identified structural vulnerabilities are addressed through planned maintenance and improvement programs.
Supply chain buffer management strategies including maintaining strategic raw material inventory buffers are implemented to absorb supply disruptions caused by climate events affecting key suppliers.
Alternate supplier identification and qualification is conducted for critical raw materials to reduce single-source supply chain climate vulnerability.

steps.heading: A documented Climate Change Recovery Plan (Business Continuity Plan) is maintained

body.text: A documented Climate Change Recovery Plan (Business Continuity Plan) is maintained identifying critical business functions, recovery priorities, alternative operational arrangements, communication protocols, and responsible personnel for climate-related disruption scenarios.

steps.heading: The Recovery Plan covers specific scenarios

body.text: The Recovery Plan covers specific scenarios including major flooding, cyclone impact, extended power disruption, and supply chain disruption, with specific response and recovery procedures for each scenario.

steps.heading: Recovery plan responsibilities are formally assigned

body.text: Recovery plan responsibilities are formally assigned to named individuals and departments with clear escalation protocols and emergency contact lists.

steps.heading: The Recovery Plan is reviewed and tested

body.text: The Recovery Plan is reviewed and tested through tabletop exercises minimum annually and updated based on exercise findings or operational changes.

blocks.text:
Workers and management receive awareness training on climate risk preparedness, emergency procedures for flood and cyclone events, heat stress recognition and prevention, and their role in the Business Continuity Plan.
Real-time weather monitoring services, Bangladesh Meteorological Department alerts, and cyclone warning systems are utilized to provide advance notice of potential climate events for proactive operational response.
Climate risk management performance and recovery plan status are reviewed in management review meetings with improvement recommendations incorporated into operational plans.

Climate physical risk management practices comply with Bangladesh Disaster Management Act, applicable building safety codes, and environmental risk management requirements. Business continuity plans and emergency response procedures are aligned with Bangladesh Meteorological Department early warning system protocols. Climate risk documentation is maintained for sustainability reporting, buyer sustainability assessments, and internal governance reviews.

The Company plans to commission a formal third-party climate vulnerability assessment to comprehensively evaluate site-specific climate exposure over 10-year and 25-year horizons. Future initiatives include installation of automated flood detection sensors and alert systems, development of climate-linked insurance coverage for critical assets, and integration of climate risk criteria into supplier qualification processes to strengthen supply chain resilience against climate-related disruptions.

narrative.text: Climate risk indicators including seasonal flood preparedness inspection results, heat stress incident occurrences, supply chain disruption events, and business continuity plan exercise outcomes are reviewed annually by management. Weather monitoring records and emergency response activations are documented and reviewed after each event. The Climate Physical Risk SOP is reviewed and updated annually incorporating lessons learned from any climate-related operational disruptions experienced during the year.

sops.title: SUSTAINABLE ENERGY MANAGEMENT & GREENHOUSE GAS REDUCTION

blocks.text: Padma Satel Arab Fashion Ltd. is committed to minimizing energy consumption and greenhouse gas emissions through systematic energy efficiency improvement, responsible energy procurement, and structured energy performance monitoring across all facility operations. The Company has installed high energy-efficiency equipment, implemented operational energy controls, and is actively evaluating renewable energy integration as part of its long-term sustainability strategy. This SOP provides a detailed framework governing all aspects of energy management aligned with international sustainability standards and buyer sustainability assessment requirements.

This SOP applies to all energy-consuming systems within the facility including production machinery, lighting systems, HVAC, utility equipment, compressed air systems, generators, boilers, transportation functions, and all administrative operations.

rows.definition: Energy consumed per unit of production output, used as a KPI for energy efficiency improvement tracking.
The reference period energy consumption data against which improvements are measured year-on-year.
The total amount of GHG emissions caused by the Company's activities expressed in CO2 equivalent (CO2e).
Energy from naturally replenishing sources including solar, wind, and hydro power.

responsibilities: Approves energy strategy; provides investment for efficiency upgrades; reviews performance at management reviews
Oversees energy monitoring, reporting, and improvement program implementation
Manages energy-consuming equipment; implements efficiency improvements; monitors utility meters
Coordinates energy awareness training for all workers and staff
Enforce equipment shutdown practices; report abnormal consumption; follow energy-saving instructions
Follow energy conservation practices in daily operations; report observed wastage to supervisors

body.text:
A technical feasibility study has been reviewed to evaluate solar photovoltaic panel installation potential based on available rooftop area, structural load capacity, shading conditions, and grid connectivity requirements.
Financial analysis covering capital investment requirements, estimated payback period, Bangladesh government incentives, net-metering availability, and return on investment has been reviewed by management.
Regulatory requirements for renewable energy installation including approvals from Bangladesh Power Development Board and relevant local authorities are identified as part of the feasibility process.

Where renewable energy systems are installed, they are commissioned by certified technical vendors with documented compliance to applicable electrical safety standards.
Monthly renewable energy generation data is recorded and compared against baseline electricity consumption to measure emission reduction impact and track renewable energy share percentage.
Preventive maintenance schedules for renewable energy systems are established and followed to ensure long-term operational efficiency and reliability.

Comprehensive energy performance assessments are conducted periodically minimum every two years or more frequently where significant energy efficiency concerns are identified.
Energy assessments cover all significant energy-consuming systems including production machinery, lighting, HVAC, compressed air, boilers, and generators to identify inefficiency areas.
Assessment findings are documented with prioritized improvement recommendations, estimated savings, implementation cost estimates, payback periods, and designated responsible departments.
Management reviews assessment reports and incorporates prioritized recommendations into capital expenditure planning and operational improvement programs.

LED lighting systems compliant with applicable energy efficiency standards have been installed throughout all operational areas replacing conventional fluorescent and incandescent lighting.
Post-installation electricity savings from LED upgrades are measured and documented by comparing monthly consumption data before and after installation.
Lighting controls including occupancy sensors in low-traffic areas and zonal lighting switches are implemented to minimize unnecessary energy consumption during unoccupied periods.
Replaced conventional lighting components are disposed of responsibly through authorized waste management channels in compliance with applicable environmental regulations.

HVAC systems in administrative areas and comfort-conditioned spaces are maintained under regular preventive maintenance programs including filter cleaning, refrigerant checks, and system efficiency testing.
Temperature set-points for air-conditioned areas are managed at energy-efficient levels. Staff are trained to avoid unnecessary cooling in unoccupied spaces.
HVAC system operation is scheduled to align with occupied hours and shut down outside working hours to avoid unnecessary energy waste.
Production floor ventilation is managed through industrial fans and natural ventilation systems to maintain worker thermal comfort while minimizing electricity consumption.

Company vehicle operations and worker transportation are managed to minimize fuel consumption and greenhouse gas emissions through route optimization and load consolidation practices.
Regular preventive maintenance of all company-operated vehicles and transportation equipment is performed per documented maintenance schedules to maintain fuel efficiency.
Fuel consumption data for all company vehicles is recorded monthly, reviewed for abnormal trends, and used for GHG emission calculations and sustainability reporting.
Shared worker transportation arrangements are managed efficiently to reduce per-capita emissions and minimize unnecessary vehicle trips.

sections.title: Workforce Training on Energy and Carbon Reduction

blocks.text:
All workers and staff receive annual awareness training covering energy conservation practices, the connection between energy use and climate change, the Company's energy targets, and practical energy-saving behaviors applicable to their specific work activities.
Training content includes switching off idle equipment and lighting when leaving work areas; reporting unusual machinery sounds or excessive heat indicating efficiency problems; optimizing machine settings to avoid energy waste.
New employees receive energy conservation awareness as part of their comprehensive induction training program before commencing independent work.
Department-specific energy conservation practices are incorporated into work instructions for key equipment operations in each department.
Training attendance records and energy awareness documentation are maintained by HR for audit verification purposes.

The Company monitors internationally recognized voluntary carbon offset mechanisms and verified carbon credit programs as part of its long-term climate strategy.
Opportunities for carbon offset procurement from credible projects registered under recognized voluntary standards are evaluated during annual sustainability planning reviews.
The Company's primary focus remains on direct operational emission reductions through energy efficiency, with carbon offset procurement considered a complementary long-term measure.

Energy management activities comply with applicable Bangladesh Energy Regulatory Commission guidelines, DoE environmental reporting requirements, and conditions of the Company's Environmental Clearance Certificate. GHG emission data is calculated and reported using recognized international emission factor methodologies. Energy consumption and emission records are retained for minimum 5 years for regulatory and audit verification purposes.

Planned future energy initiatives include installation of solar photovoltaic panels on available rooftop areas to generate on-site clean electricity, implementation of a real-time digital energy monitoring system providing department-level consumption visibility, exploration of green electricity procurement options from utility providers, investment in additional VFD installations across remaining motor systems, and development of a formal carbon reduction roadmap with specific emission reduction milestones for coming years.

narrative.text: Monthly energy consumption data by source (electricity, diesel, gas) and calculated GHG emissions (Scope 1 and Scope 2) are reviewed by the EHS/Sustainability Officer and compared against set targets. Energy intensity ratios (energy per unit production) are tracked to separate efficiency improvements from production volume changes. Quarterly energy performance summaries are presented to senior management. The Sustainable Energy Management SOP is reviewed annually.

blocks.text: Padma Satel Arab Fashion Ltd. is committed to responsible materials and chemical management to ensure environmental protection, worker health and safety, regulatory compliance, and operational efficiency across all production and support activities. As a garment manufacturer the Company utilizes a range of raw materials including fabric, accessories, threads, finishing chemicals, dyes, adhesives, and maintenance chemicals. This SOP establishes a structured framework for material efficiency, responsible chemical procurement, restricted substance compliance, environmental incident response, and worker chemical safety training.

This SOP applies to all production floors, cutting sections, finishing areas, chemical storage rooms, maintenance workshops, ETP operations, and logistics activities where materials and chemicals are procured, stored, handled, used, or disposed of. It covers all employees and contractors engaged in material and chemical management activities.

Quantity of raw material consumed per unit of production output used for efficiency tracking.

body.text: Production and operational processes are periodically reviewed to identify areas of excessive material consumption, abnormal reject rates, rework volumes, spillage, or process inefficiencies contributing to avoidable material waste.

Fabric spreading plans and marker efficiency optimization are applied to minimize fabric cutting waste in the cutting section. Marker efficiency rates are monitored and improvement targets applied continuously.
Standard operating parameters for chemical usage in finishing and production processes are documented and followed to ensure consistent and optimized material utilization across all production lines.
Recyclable scrap materials including fabric offcuts, thread waste, and carton waste are segregated and directed to authorized recyclers or repurposed internally where technically feasible.
Monthly material consumption data is monitored against production output to calculate material intensity ratios and track efficiency improvements over time.

sections.title: 6.2 Restricted Substances and Sustainable Materials Compliance

body.text: All chemicals used in production including dyes, finishing chemicals, softeners, and adhesives are verified against applicable Restricted Substances Lists before procurement approval is granted.
Suppliers are required to provide current MSDS/SDS documents, compliance declarations, and relevant test certifications for all chemical products supplied prior to authorized use in production.

Materials with lower environmental impact, reduced chemical content, improved recyclability, or certified sustainable sourcing are evaluated and prioritized during procurement decisions where technically feasible.
The chemical inventory is reviewed quarterly to identify products requiring substitution with less hazardous or more environmentally preferable alternatives.
All hazardous chemicals are stored in designated, properly labeled, adequately ventilated, and restricted-access chemical storage areas with appropriate secondary containment systems.
Incompatible chemicals such as acids and bases, oxidizers and flammables, are stored in physically separate areas following chemical compatibility requirements to prevent dangerous reactions.
Chemical containers are clearly labeled with product name, hazard symbols, handling precautions, and emergency contact information in Bengali and English.
First-In First-Out (FIFO) stock rotation is applied in chemical storage to prevent product expiry and minimize waste.
Workers handling hazardous materials wear appropriate PPE as identified in the risk assessment and MSDS for each chemical. PPE compliance is actively monitored by supervisors.
Spill response kits including absorbent materials, neutralizers, and containment barriers are available in all chemical handling areas and workers are trained on their correct use.
Any employee observing a chemical spill, hazardous leak, fire event, or potential environmental hazard immediately reports to their supervisor and the EHS Officer without delay.
Environmental incident reports are completed within 24 hours of occurrence using the standard incident report form maintained by the EHS department.

Trained emergency response personnel use available spill kits, absorbent materials, and containment barriers to immediately prevent spread of spilled chemicals to drainage systems, soil, or water bodies.
Worker evacuation from the immediate spill area is initiated if the incident poses acute health risks from chemical vapor, fire, or explosion hazard.
The affected area is isolated and restricted until the spill is fully contained and cleaned up to prevent secondary exposure of other workers.
Root cause analysis is conducted within 72 hours of the incident to determine underlying causes and identify specific preventive measures to avoid recurrence.
Corrective actions including procedure updates, additional engineering controls, retraining, or equipment repair are implemented with defined owners and completion dates.
Bangladesh Department of Environment is notified in cases where the incident results in environmental release or pollution in violation of applicable regulations.

blocks.text: All new workers handling chemicals receive mandatory chemical safety induction training before commencing independent work covering hazard identification, SDS interpretation, GHS pictograms, PPE selection, and emergency response procedures.
Annual refresher training on chemical safety is conducted for all operational and maintenance staff with documented attendance records maintained by HR.
Emergency response team members receive specialized chemical emergency response training and participate in annual mock drill exercises.
Post-training competency assessments are conducted to verify adequate knowledge retention.

All material and chemical management activities comply with Bangladesh Environment Conservation Act, Hazardous Waste Management Rules, OSHA-aligned occupational safety regulations, and applicable international chemical safety standards including GHS classification requirements. Compliance with buyer Restricted Substances Lists is maintained through documented supplier declarations and periodic laboratory testing. Chemical inventory records, MSDS files, incident reports, disposal records, and training attendance documentation are maintained for minimum 5 years.

The Company plans to implement a digital chemical management system to enable real-time tracking of chemical inventory, usage, and compliance status across all departments. Future initiatives include transitioning to lower-hazard chemical alternatives for finishing and maintenance operations, engaging with certified sustainable chemistry programs, expanding laboratory testing protocols for RSL verification, and developing a formal Chemical Reduction Roadmap with quantitative targets for reducing the number and volume of hazardous chemicals used in production processes.

narrative.text: Chemical inventory compliance is audited quarterly by the EHS Officer covering MSDS completeness, storage compliance, RSL verification status, and disposal record accuracy. Material efficiency indicators including marker efficiency rates, fabric waste percentages, and chemical consumption intensity are tracked monthly. Incident reports and near-miss records related to chemical handling are reviewed monthly by the Safety Committee. The Materials and Chemicals Management SOP is reviewed annually.

sops.title: WASTE MANAGEMENT, RECYCLING & CIRCULAR ECONOMY PRACTICES

blocks.text:
Padma Satel Arab Fashion Ltd. (hereinafter referred to as 'the Company' or 'PSA Fashion') is a leading woven and knit garment manufacturer based in Bangladesh, supplying high-quality apparel to international buyers across Europe, North America, and global markets. As a responsible manufacturer committed to environmental sustainability, the Company recognizes that effective waste management is a fundamental obligation not only for regulatory compliance, but for the protection of environmental quality, worker health, community well-being, and long-term business sustainability.

This Standard Operating Procedure (SOP) establishes the comprehensive framework governing the identification, categorization, segregation, collection, storage, recovery, recycling, and disposal of all waste streams generated from the Company's manufacturing operations, utility systems, canteen activities, and administrative functions. It applies the principles of the Circular Economy maximizing material value, minimizing waste generation, and ensuring that all unavoidable waste is managed in the most environmentally responsible manner available.

This SOP is aligned with the requirements of ISO 14001:2015 Environmental Management System, Eco Vadis environmental assessment criteria, Bangladesh Environment Conservation Act and Rules, Department of Environment (DoE) waste management regulations, and applicable customer and certification body requirements including BSCI, SEDEX, GOTS, and OEKO-TEX. Compliance with this SOP is mandatory for all employees, contractors, and service providers operating within Company premises.

This SOP applies to the following:

Waste Streams Covered

All fabric and textile waste including off-cuts, clippings, thread waste, and defective fabric from cutting, sewing, and finishing operations
Chemical waste, used chemical containers, expired chemicals, solvents, and chemical-contaminated materials
ETP (Effluent Treatment Plant) sludge and chemical treatment residues from wastewater management operations
Packaging waste including cardboard cartons, polybags, plastic straps, foam, and wrapping materials
General and organic waste from canteen, offices, and administrative areas
E-waste including expired electrical equipment, batteries, printer cartridges, and electronic components
Hazardous waste requiring licensed disposal as classified under Bangladesh DoE regulations
Departments Covered

Production — Spreading, Cutting, Sewing, Finishing, Washing, Packing
Utility — Boiler Room, Effluent Treatment Plant (ETP), Generator Room, Compressor Area
Quality & Laboratory — Chemical testing, fabric inspection, sample rooms
Warehouse & Stores — Raw material storage, finished goods, accessories
Maintenance — Mechanical, electrical, and civil maintenance operations
Administration — Offices, canteen, HR, and administration areas

blocks.text:
Circular Economy Commitments

The Company applies the following circular economy principles to reduce its environmental footprint and maximize material value:

Cutting Marker Optimization: Production planning teams optimize fabric cutting markers to maximize material utilization and minimize fabric off-cut waste per production order.
Defect Rate Reduction: Systematic quality improvement programs reduce fabric rejection rates, directly reducing waste generation from defective materials.
Internal Fabric Reuse: Usable fabric remnants and off cuts are identified and reserved for sample making, prototype development, and training activities before classification as waste.
Packaging Material Recovery: Incoming cardboard cartons and packaging materials are collected, compacted, and transferred to authorized paper and plastic recyclers for material recovery.
Chemical Optimization: Precise chemical dosing systems and batch management reduce chemical waste generation from over-ordering, expired stock, and residual chemical disposal.
Steam Condensate Recovery: Steam condensate returned to the boiler feed water system reduces both water and energy waste from the utility operation.
Supplier Collaboration: The Company works with key fabric and material suppliers to explore returnable packaging, take-back programs, and reduced packaging options as part of supply chain circular economy improvement.

body.text: PSA Fashion uses a standardized seven-color bin system deployed throughout all operational areas to ensure consistent, error-free waste segregation at the point of generation. All bins are clearly labeled in both Bengali and English with color coding and pictograms:

rows: Chemical waste, used chemical containers, contaminated rags, expired chemicals
ETP sludge, filter cake, chemical treatment residues
Paper, cardboard boxes, cartons, documents for shredding
Food waste, canteen waste, non-recyclable general municipal waste
Polybags, plastic straps, plastic packaging, plastic waste

body.text: Bin placements are mapped and updated whenever operational layouts change. A minimum of one complete set of color-coded bins is stationed at every 15-meter interval on production floors, and individual bins are placed at point-source locations such as cutting tables, chemical handling areas, canteen serving areas, and chemical storage zones.

Waste must be segregated at the point of generation without delay waste that has been mixed with a different category must not be manually separated afterwards; the mixed waste is classified as the highest hazard category present.
Workers must place each piece of waste into the correct color-coded bin immediately upon generation; cross-contamination between bins of different categories is classified as a segregation non-conformance.
Full bins are sealed, labeled with generation date and department, and moved to the intermediate waste storage area by the designated bin handler; full bins are never left unattended in production areas.
All waste bins are inspected by supervisors at least twice per shift; incorrectly segregated waste identified during inspection is photographed, the non-conformance is recorded, and the responsible worker receives immediate retraining.
No waste of any category is to be disposed of in drainage channels, open ground areas, roof areas, or any undesignated location within or outside the Company premises.

Fabric off-cuts, clippings, and thread waste generated at sewing workstations are placed into the designated purple textile waste collection bags attached to each sewing machine stand; bags are replaced when 80% full.
Cutting room waste including large fabric off cuts is collected in designated purple textile waste skips positioned alongside each cutting table; cutting supervisors ensure correct segregation of synthetic, natural, and organic fabric waste streams.
Accessory waste including broken buttons, defective zippers, faulty labels, and unusable trim materials is segregated into labeled general waste bins unless classified as hazardous, in which case the red bin applies.
Rejected garments and defective finished goods are stored separately in labeled hold areas for management disposition rework, donation, or authorized disposal and are not mixed with fabric or thread waste.

Chemical waste is never mixed with general waste, fabric waste, or any other waste stream; all chemical waste including residues, expired chemicals, and contaminated materials is placed exclusively in red bins with secure lids.
Empty chemical containers are triple-rinsed where the SDS permits water rinsing, drained completely, recapped, and placed in designated red chemical container collection areas separate from other chemical waste.
Used lubricants, hydraulic oils, and maintenance oils are collected in dedicated sealed metal drums stored in the maintenance chemical storage area; these are never poured into drains or mixed with other waste.
Chemical spill absorbent materials used during spill cleanup are treated as chemical waste and disposed of through the licensed hazardous waste route; they are not placed in general waste bins.

Office paper, printed documents, and cardboard packaging materials are collected in blue bins; confidential documents are placed in secure shredding boxes and shredded on-site before transfer to paper recyclers.
Canteen food waste and organic materials are segregated into green bins; canteen operators ensure liquid food waste is drained before bin collection to prevent leakage and odor during transport.
Plastic cups, cutlery, and soft drink packaging from canteen areas are collected in yellow bins where clean and non-contaminated; food-contaminated plastics are placed in green general waste bins.
E-waste and batteries from offices and administration are collected in designated grey bins located in the IT department and administration area; batteries are never placed in general or chemical waste streams.

All new employees receive mandatory waste segregation training as part of their induction program before commencing work, covering the color-coded bin system, waste categories, segregation rules, and non-conformance consequences.
Annual refresher waste segregation training is conducted for all employees through toolbox talks, departmental briefings, and visual awareness campaigns including posters and digital displays.
Waste segregation awareness posters with color-coded visual guides and prohibited actions are displayed in Bengali and English at all bin locations, chemical storage areas, production floors, and canteen areas.
Monthly waste segregation inspection scores are shared with department heads and posted on department notice boards to promote awareness and healthy competition between departments.

blocks.text: Hazardous waste management at PSA Fashion follows strictly controlled procedures to ensure that all hazardous materials are identified, segregated, safely stored, tracked through a complete manifest system, and disposed of exclusively through DoE-licensed and authorized waste contractors. No hazardous waste is disposed of through general waste streams, municipal collection, open burning, or drainage systems under any circumstances.

body.text: The following table provides the complete hazardous waste classification for PSA Fashion's operations:

rows: Labeled sealed containers in bunded secondary containment area
Labeled sealed drums in hazardous storage
Return to supplier or licensed disposal
Sealed skip or container in designated sludge area
Sealed metal drums in maintenance store

body.text:
Hazardous waste is stored in a designated Hazardous Waste Storage Area that is physically separated from general waste, chemical stores, production areas, and personnel facilities.
The Hazardous Waste Storage Area features bunded concrete flooring with containment capacity equal to 110% of the largest container volume, preventing soil or groundwater contamination from spills or container failure.
The storage area is clearly marked with hazard warning signs (Skull & Crossbones, Corrosive, Flammable as applicable), kept locked when not in use, and accessible only to EHS and authorized personnel.
Adequate ventilation is maintained in the hazardous waste storage area to prevent accumulation of flammable or toxic vapors from stored chemical waste containers.
Each hazardous waste container is labeled with waste type, hazard classification, date generated, generator department, responsible person, and storage start date using the Company's standardized hazardous waste label template.
Hazardous waste containers are inspected weekly for leakage, corrosion, label integrity, and secure closure; any container showing signs of deterioration is immediately transferred to a new sound container with documentation.
Maximum storage period limits are enforced for each hazardous waste type (as specified in the table above); waste approaching storage limit is prioritized for next scheduled disposal to prevent regulatory non-compliance.
Fire extinguishers appropriate for chemical fires (CO2 and dry powder types) are stationed adjacent to the hazardous waste storage area and are inspected monthly by EHS personnel.

A Hazardous Waste Register is maintained by the EHS team recording all hazardous waste types, quantities generated, storage dates, disposal dates, contractor details, manifest numbers, and disposal verification.
A Waste Manifest (WTN - Waste Transfer Note) is completed for every hazardous waste transfer from the Company to a licensed waste contractor, covering waste type, hazard classification, quantity, packaging, and contractor license details.
Original signed copies of all waste manifests and disposal certificates are retained by the EHS team for a minimum period of five years for regulatory inspection and EcoVadis audit verification purposes.
Transportation of hazardous waste from the Company's premises is conducted exclusively by licensed hazardous waste transporters with valid DoE permits, appropriate transportation equipment, and emergency response capability.
Upon completion of hazardous waste disposal, the EHS team verifies receipt of a signed disposal certificate or confirmation from the licensed contractor confirming the waste has been treated or disposed of in an environmentally sound manner.

ETP sludge is generated from the physical, chemical, and biological treatment stages of PSA Fashion's Effluent Treatment Plant and is classified as a controlled waste requiring specific management under Bangladesh DoE regulations.
ETP sludge is dewatered using filter presses or drying beds within the ETP facility before storage and transfer, reducing water content and volume for more efficient and compliant disposal.
Sludge quantity is measured and recorded at each dewatering cycle; monthly sludge generation totals are reported in the environmental performance data register and included in EcoVadis environmental data submissions.
ETP sludge is stored in covered, labeled, sealed skips or containers in the designated sludge storage area, segregated from other hazardous and general waste, for a maximum of 30 days before scheduled disposal.
DoE-licensed sludge disposal contractors are engaged through formal contracts specifying collection schedules, licensed disposal facilities, documentation requirements, and performance standards.
In the event of a chemical spill or hazardous waste release, the following immediate response procedure is followed:

STOP — Cease any activity that is contributing to the spill or release; activate emergency alarm if spill is significant.
ALERT — Immediately notify the EHS Officer and floor supervisor; evacuate non-essential personnel from the affected area.
CONTAIN — Using the nearest spill response kit (located at all chemical handling points), deploy absorbent materials or booms to contain the spill and prevent it from reaching drains.
PROTECT — Don appropriate PPE (chemical-resistant gloves, goggles, apron, and respiratory protection as indicated by the SDS) before entering the spill area.
CLEAN UP — Absorb, neutralize (if applicable per SDS), and collect all spilled material and contaminated absorbents into sealed labeled hazardous waste containers.
DOCUMENT — Record the incident in the environmental incident register: date, time, location, chemical type, estimated quantity, response actions, and personnel involved.
INVESTIGATE — Conduct root cause analysis within 48 hours; implement corrective actions; review spill kit adequacy and response training within 7 days.

blocks.text: PSA Fashion manages the recovery and recycling of all recyclable waste streams through formally contracted, licensed, and periodically verified authorized recycling partners. The use of unauthorized collectors or informal waste buyers without verifiable licensing is strictly prohibited for all waste categories.

rows: Licensed textile recycler or authorized resale buyer
Licensed used oil re-refinery or recycler

body.text:
All waste collection and recycling contractors must hold valid and current DoE environmental permits, business licenses, and (where applicable) hazardous waste transportation permits before being added to the Company's Approved Contractor List.
New recycling contractors undergo a formal qualification process including submission of copies of all relevant licenses, a Company-conducted site assessment visit (for hazardous waste contractors), and signing of the Company's Contractor Code of Conduct.
The license validity and environmental compliance status of all authorized recyclers is verified on a defined periodic basis (annually for general recyclers, semi-annually for hazardous waste contractors) and records are maintained by the EHS team.
Recyclers who are found to have expired or revoked licenses, whose facilities are subject to regulatory enforcement, or who fail to provide required waste transfer documentation are immediately suspended from the Approved Contractor List.
Preferred recycler status is awarded to contractors who demonstrate consistent performance, complete documentation, transparent reporting, and active improvement in their own environmental management practices.

For every waste transfer to an authorized recycler or disposal contractor, the following minimum documentation is obtained and filed: completed and signed Waste Transfer Note (WTN), weight slip or scale receipt confirming quantity transferred, and contractor's license copy (retained on first engagement and upon renewal).
For all hazardous waste transfers, an additional Hazardous Waste Manifest is required covering full chain-of-custody from generator (PSA Fashion) to final disposal or treatment facility, signed by all parties in the chain.
Upon completion of hazardous or regulated waste disposal, a Disposal Completion Certificate or Treatment Confirmation from the licensed facility must be received, reviewed, and filed by the EHS team within 30 days of transfer.
All waste transfer records are maintained in a structured Waste Records File organized by waste category and month; records are retained for a minimum of five years and are made available for internal audit, EcoVadis submission, DoE inspection, and BSCI or SEDEX social audit verification.
The Waste Register is reconciled monthly by the EHS team, comparing generation quantities, transfer records, and disposal certificates to verify the completeness and accuracy of the waste management record trail.

narrative.text: PSA Fashion maintains a comprehensive waste monitoring and reporting system to track waste generation performance, measure progress against reduction targets, identify improvement opportunities, and demonstrate environmental compliance to regulatory bodies, certification auditors, and customers including through the EcoVadis annual assessment.

Waste generation quantities for all waste streams are measured and recorded monthly using weighbridge records, transfer note quantities, and internal bin count measurements; data is consolidated in the monthly Environmental Performance Data Register.
Waste intensity ratios (kg of waste per unit of production output) are calculated monthly for fabric waste and total non-hazardous waste to enable meaningful comparison of waste generation performance across periods of different production volumes.
Abnormal increases in waste generation for any category defined as more than 20% above the 3-month rolling average trigger a mandatory investigation by the EHS team within 7 days to identify root causes and implement corrective actions.
Hazardous waste generation quantities, storage periods, disposal dates, and contractor details are tracked separately in the Hazardous Waste Register and reconciled against disposal manifests and certificates monthly.

Monthly waste segregation compliance audits are conducted by the EHS Officer across all departments and operational areas; audit scores are calculated for each area and shared with department heads within 5 working days of the audit date.
Quarterly comprehensive waste management system audits assess all elements of this SOP including waste identification, bin system effectiveness, hazardous waste storage compliance, recycler documentation, and training records.
Annual waste management system reviews are conducted by management, assessing performance against annual targets, reviewing the waste contractor approved list, updating the waste stream register, and setting improvement objectives for the following year.
Waste audit findings and non-conformances are tracked through the Company's CAPA system; corrective actions are assigned with specific owners and completion timelines and verified for effectiveness at the next audit cycle.

sops.title: RESPONSIBLE SOURCING, ETHICAL PROCUREMENT & SUPPLY CHAIN INTEGRITY

blocks.text: Padma Satel Arab Fashion Ltd. recognizes that responsible sourcing and supply chain integrity are fundamental to sustainable business operations and maintaining the trust of international customers. The Company implements systematic procedures for supplier qualification, ethical procurement, supply chain due diligence, and subcontractor management to ensure that all suppliers and subcontractors uphold standards equivalent to those applied within its own operations. Responsible sourcing is integrated into all procurement decision-making and supplier relationship management activities.

This SOP applies to all procurement activities, supplier relationships, subcontracting arrangements, and material and service sourcing decisions. It covers fabric mills, trim and accessory suppliers, chemical suppliers, packaging suppliers, logistics providers, and all other service providers engaged by the Company.

rows.definition: Any external entity providing goods, raw materials, accessories, chemicals, packaging, or services to the Company.
An external facility performing any production process step on behalf of the Company.
A systematic process of assessing and managing ESG risks within the supply chain.
A document setting out the Company's minimum expectations for ethical, labor, environmental, and governance performance from all suppliers.

responsibilities: Leads supplier qualification, manages supplier relationships, ensures CoC compliance documentation
Reviews supplier ESG performance, manages supply chain audit program, tracks corrective actions
Evaluates supplier quality capability and technical performance standards
Reviews payment terms compliance and financial integrity of procurement transactions
Approves strategic supplier relationships and responsible sourcing policy

body.text:
New suppliers are evaluated against defined qualification criteria covering legal registration, labor standard compliance, environmental practices, product quality capability, and business ethics before receiving approved supplier status.
All new suppliers are required to complete a Supplier Self-Assessment Questionnaire (SAQ) covering labor practices, health and safety, environmental management, and anti-corruption compliance before approval.
Supporting documentation including business registration certificates, factory compliance certificates, relevant audit reports, and certifications are collected and verified during the onboarding process.
A Supplier Code of Conduct is formally shared with all suppliers during onboarding. Written acknowledgment and commitment to compliance is obtained from supplier management before the first order is placed.
An Approved Supplier Register is maintained listing all qualified suppliers with their approval status, product/service categories, compliance documentation status, and performance evaluation history.

Strict prohibition of child labor, forced labor, bonded labor, and all forms of human trafficking in supplier operations and their own supply chains.
Payment of wages meeting or exceeding applicable minimum wage requirements; payment on time and in full without unauthorized deductions.
Compliance with applicable working hours laws; overtime strictly voluntary and compensated at applicable premium rates with worker consent.
Provision of safe, healthy, and hygienic working conditions for all workers with emergency preparedness measures and access to first aid services.
Non-discrimination in employment; maintenance of respectful, harassment-free workplaces for all workers.
Compliance with applicable environmental regulations including waste management, chemical handling, and pollution prevention requirements.
Zero tolerance for bribery, corruption, and unethical business practices in all commercial transactions.
Suppliers are required to extend the same standards to their own sub-suppliers and subcontractors where relevant.

All subcontracting of any production process is documented and disclosed to relevant customers as required by applicable commercial agreements and buyer codes of conduct.
Subcontractors are assessed against the same qualification and compliance criteria as direct suppliers before receiving authorization to process the Company's production orders.
Authorized subcontractor facilities are subject to periodic compliance assessments covering labor, safety, and environmental requirements minimum annually or following identified concerns.
Unauthorized subcontracting or transfer of production to facilities not approved through the Company's qualification process is strictly prohibited and subject to immediate corrective action.
Subcontractor records including approval status, assessment findings, non-conformances, and corrective action status are maintained and reviewed quarterly.

Supplier performance reviews are conducted at minimum annually covering product quality, delivery performance, documentation compliance, and sustainability performance indicators.
Supplier compliance documentation, audit results, non-conformance records, corrective action status, and certification validity are tracked in a centralized supplier performance system.
Critical and strategic suppliers are subject to more frequent performance reviews and may be required to implement targeted improvement programs with defined timelines.
Persistent non-compliance with Code of Conduct requirements may result in formal corrective action requirements, supplier probation status, or relationship termination where improvement is not achieved.

The Company maintains awareness of material sourcing risks including conflict minerals and other supply chain integrity risks as applicable to textile supply chains.
Key material suppliers are requested to provide information on material geographic origin and sourcing practices to support product traceability requirements from international buyers.
Material traceability documentation and responsible sourcing data is maintained for sustainability reporting, customer disclosure requirements, and sustainability assessments.

blocks.text:
Procurement and sourcing personnel receive annual training covering the Supplier Code of Conduct, responsible sourcing requirements, supplier evaluation procedures, and recognition of supply chain risk indicators.
Training content includes identification of child labor, forced labor, and environmental non-compliance indicators during supplier visits, documentation reviews, or audit processes.
Training records for procurement and sourcing staff are documented and maintained with competency assessment results updated annually.

All supply chain management activities comply with Bangladesh labour and environmental laws as applicable to supply chain relationships, and with the responsible sourcing and subcontracting requirements of the Company's international buyer Codes of Conduct. Supplier qualification records, SAQ responses, Code of Conduct acknowledgments, subcontractor authorization records, and supplier performance evaluation documents are maintained for minimum 5 years and are made available during buyer and third-party audits.

The Company plans to implement a formal supplier sustainability development program providing training and capacity building support to key suppliers on labor standards, environmental management, and anti-corruption practices. Future initiatives include introduction of a digital supplier compliance portal for streamlined document collection and performance tracking, expansion of supplier auditing to cover all Tier 2 key material suppliers, and development of a formal Sustainable Procurement Policy approved at Board level.

narrative.text: Supplier compliance status is reviewed quarterly by the Procurement and Compliance teams. The Approved Supplier Register is updated with compliance status, audit findings, and corrective action progress at each quarterly review. Annual supply chain risk assessments identify high-risk suppliers for enhanced due diligence. The Responsible Sourcing SOP is reviewed annually incorporating lessons from supplier audit findings, customer feedback on supply chain requirements, and updates to applicable international standards.

blocks.text: Padma Satel Arab Fashion Ltd. is committed to conducting all business operations with the highest standards of integrity, transparency, and ethical conduct. The Company maintains absolute zero tolerance for corruption, bribery, fraud, kickbacks, facilitation payments, and any form of unethical business practice across all operations, supply chain relationships, and business interactions. This SOP establishes comprehensive procedures for preventing, detecting, and responding to corruption risks within the organization and in all external business relationships.

This SOP applies to all employees, management personnel, board members, agents, consultants, and third parties acting on behalf of Padma Satel Arab Fashion Ltd. in any capacity. It covers all business interactions including procurement, sales, customer relations, government dealings, supplier management, and all financial transactions.

rows.definition: The offering, giving, receiving, or soliciting of anything of value to improperly influence a business or official decision.
The act of offering, giving, or receiving a benefit to influence the actions of an official or decision-maker.
An unofficial payment made to expedite a routine government or administrative action. Strictly prohibited.
A situation where a personal or financial interest may improperly influence professional responsibilities.

responsibilities: Oversight and leadership of the anti-corruption compliance framework; setting and modeling a culture of integrity

Periodic compliance verification; high-risk transaction review; findings reporting to management
