steps.heading: All forms of bribery, corruption, kickbacks, facilitation payments, fraud, and other financial misconduct are strictly prohibited

body.text: All forms of bribery, corruption, kickbacks, facilitation payments, fraud, and other financial misconduct are strictly prohibited within all Company operations and business relationships without any exception.

steps.heading: The Anti-Corruption and Business Ethics Policy is formally documented

body.text: The Anti-Corruption and Business Ethics Policy is formally documented, signed by the Managing Director, prominently displayed in facility common areas, and communicated to all employees during induction and annual refresher programs.

steps.heading: All employees are required to complete mandatory annual anti-corruption awareness training

body.text: All employees are required to complete mandatory annual anti-corruption awareness training and formally acknowledge their understanding and continuing commitment to the Policy.

steps.heading: Employees who witness, suspect, or are approached with requests for corrupt payments

body.text: Employees who witness, suspect, or are approached with requests for corrupt payments are required to report the matter immediately through formal reporting channels.

steps.heading: Violations of anti-corruption policy are subject to serious disciplinary action

body.text: Violations of anti-corruption policy are subject to serious disciplinary action including immediate termination of employment and referral to legal authorities for prosecution where warranted.

steps.heading: The Compliance Officer conducts annual corruption risk assessments

body.text: The Compliance Officer conducts annual corruption risk assessments covering all business functions with significant corruption exposure including procurement, vendor selection, regulatory approvals, customs clearance, and sales agent management.

steps.heading: Identified risks are classified by severity

body.text: Identified risks are classified by severity: High Risk (government interaction, high-value contracts, third-party intermediaries), Medium Risk (recurring vendor payments, distributor incentives), and Low Risk (standardized transactions with established internal controls).

steps.heading: For each identified risk, specific internal controls are defined

body.text: For each identified risk, specific internal controls are defined including approval hierarchies, documentation requirements, segregation of duties, and transaction monitoring procedures.

steps.heading: Risk assessment results are documented in a Corruption Risk Register

body.text: Risk assessment results are documented in a Corruption Risk Register reviewed and updated annually.

steps.heading: Employees are not permitted to accept gifts, hospitality, entertainment, or personal benefits

body.text: Employees are not permitted to accept gifts, hospitality, entertainment, or personal benefits from suppliers, customers, contractors, or government officials that could create actual or perceived obligation or conflict of interest.

steps.heading: Token, culturally appropriate business courtesies of nominal value may be accepted

body.text: Token, culturally appropriate business courtesies of nominal value may be accepted only if not linked to any pending business decision, disclosed to the supervisor, and recorded in the Gift and Hospitality Register.

steps.heading: Offering gifts, cash, entertainment, travel, or personal benefits to government officials is prohibited

body.text: Offering gifts, cash, entertainment, travel, or personal benefits to government officials or procurement decision-makers for the purpose of influencing decisions is strictly and absolutely prohibited.

steps.heading: The Gift and Hospitality Register is maintained by the Compliance function

body.text: The Gift and Hospitality Register is maintained by the Compliance function and reviewed quarterly for compliance monitoring and management reporting.

steps.heading: All employees are required to proactively disclose any actual, potential, or perceived conflict of interest

body.text: All employees are required to proactively disclose any actual, potential, or perceived conflict of interest to their department head or the Compliance Officer as soon as they become aware.

steps.heading: Employees with disclosed conflicts of interest are immediately recused

body.text: Employees with disclosed conflicts of interest are immediately recused from relevant decision-making processes, procurement approvals, or commercial evaluations involving the conflicting interest.

steps.heading: Conflict of interest declarations are formally documented

body.text: Conflict of interest declarations are formally documented, reviewed by the Compliance Officer, and maintained in the employee's personnel record.

steps.heading: Procurement decisions involving suppliers with relationships to Company employees

body.text: Procurement decisions involving suppliers with relationships to Company employees are subject to enhanced independent review and dual authorization requirements.

sections.title: Escalated Approval Protocol for High-Risk Transactions

steps.heading: All whistleblowers acting in good faith are fully protected from retaliation

steps.heading: All reports received are investigated promptly and confidentially

steps.heading: The Company maintains absolute confidentiality of whistleblower identities

steps.heading: All financial transactions are accurately and completely recorded

steps.heading: Falsification, alteration, or deliberate misrepresentation of business records

steps.heading: Robust internal financial controls are maintained

body.text: Robust internal financial controls are maintained to prevent unauthorized transactions, misappropriation of Company assets, and financial fraud at all levels.

steps.heading: Financial and anti-corruption records are retained for minimum 7 years

body.text: Financial and anti-corruption records are retained for minimum 7 years as required by applicable Bangladesh tax, accounting, and company law requirements.

blocks.text: Ethics and anti-corruption training is provided to all employees during induction covering the anti-corruption policy, prohibited behaviors, gift policy, conflict of interest obligations, reporting procedures, and consequences of violations.
Annual ethics refresher training for all employees covering anti-corruption considerations relevant to the garment sector and practical guidance on handling ethical dilemmas in commercial work.
Suppliers and key business partners are made aware of the Company's ethical standards through the Supplier Code of Conduct provisions and contract terms.
Ethics training completion records are maintained by HR for all employees and are always available for customer audit and sustainability assessment verification.

All anti-corruption activities comply with Bangladesh Penal Code anti-corruption provisions, the Prevention and Suppression of Corruption Act, applicable international anti-bribery standards, and the anti-corruption requirements of the Company's international buyer Codes of Conduct. Anti-corruption records including training completion registers, gift and hospitality registers, conflict of interest declarations, and investigation records are maintained for minimum 7 years.

The Company plans to implement a formal third-party ethics hotline to complement existing internal reporting mechanisms, providing workers with an independent and confidential channel for reporting concerns. Future initiatives include development of an enhanced due diligence program for high-risk third-party relationships, introduction of regular ethics culture surveys to measure employee awareness and confidence in reporting mechanisms, and periodic external reviews of the anti-corruption compliance framework by independent compliance specialists.

narrative.text: Anti-corruption compliance is reviewed annually by the Compliance Officer through the Corruption Risk Assessment process and internal audit. Training completion rates, gift register entries, conflict of interest declarations, and whistleblowing report volumes and resolution rates are tracked and reported to management quarterly. Anomalous patterns in financial transactions are reviewed by the Finance team and Internal Audit function. The Business Ethics SOP is reviewed annually.

sops.title: PRODUCT QUALITY MANAGEMENT, SAFETY COMPLIANCE & CUSTOMER SATISFACTION

blocks.text: Padma Satel Arab Fashion Ltd. is committed to delivering garment products that consistently meet customer quality specifications, safety requirements, and applicable regulatory standards. The Company maintains a systematic Quality Management System covering incoming material inspection, in-process quality control, final inspection, product safety compliance, restricted substances management, and customer feedback management. Product integrity and customer satisfaction are core operational commitments of the Company that are maintained through rigorous process controls at every production stage.

This SOP applies to all quality and product safety activities from raw material receipt through production, finishing, packing, and final shipment to customers. It covers all production lines, quality inspection teams, laboratory functions, and customer service activities.

rows.definition: Acceptable Quality Level, a statistical sampling standard for final product inspection defining acceptable defect rates for approval.
Restricted Substances List buyer or regulatory specified list of chemicals prohibited in finished garments.
Any deviation from specified product quality standards including workmanship defects, measurement deviations, appearance issues, or labeling non-conformances.
Corrective and Preventive Action - formal process for addressing identified quality non-conformances and preventing their recurrence.

responsibilities: coordinate immediate corrective actions on production lines
ensure operator training on quality standards
Ensure incoming materials meet approved specifications

steps.heading: All fabric rolls received from mills are inspected

body.text: All fabric rolls received from mills are inspected using the 4-Point fabric inspection system against approved specifications covering defect types, density, weave integrity, width, shade consistency, and shrinkage.

Accessories including buttons, zippers, interlining, labels, threads, and packaging materials are inspected against purchase order specifications and approved counter samples before release for production.

steps.heading: Incoming inspection records including lot number

body.text: Incoming inspection records including lot number, roll numbers, quantity received, defects found, pass/fail decision, and disposition action are documented in the Incoming Inspection Register.
Non-conforming materials are immediately quarantined with clear non-conformance tags, removed from the usable material flow, and processed through the supplier non-conformance reporting procedure.

steps.heading: Critical fabric or accessory lots may be subject to laboratory testing

body.text: Critical fabric or accessory lots may be subject to laboratory testing for dimensional stability, color fastness, and RSL compliance before being approved for production use.

steps.heading: Inline quality inspections are conducted at defined checkpoints

body.text: Inline quality inspections are conducted at defined checkpoints throughout the production process covering cutting accuracy, sewing quality, seam integrity, measurement compliance, and overall workmanship standards.

steps.heading: Each sewing line has assigned quality inspectors

body.text: Each sewing line has assigned quality inspectors conducting regular bundle-level and hourly line inspections. Defect rates by type and line are recorded on daily Inline Quality Control reports.

steps.heading: When defect rates exceed defined alert thresholds

body.text: When defect rates exceed defined alert thresholds, immediate corrective actions are initiated including production hold, machine adjustment, operator retraining, or line re-inspection.
Rework activities are documented and reworked garments are re-inspected before returning to the production flow to prevent defective product progression.

steps.heading: Measurement audit checks are conducted periodically

body.text: Measurement audit checks are conducted periodically by QA supervisors on finished panels and garments to verify compliance with buyer measurement specifications.

steps.heading: All finished goods are subject to comprehensive final inspection

body.text: All finished goods are subject to comprehensive final inspection using AQL sampling plans as agreed with individual customers before packing authorization is granted.

Final inspection covers workmanship quality, measurement compliance, appearance and presentation, packing standards, labelling accuracy, care instruction labels, and compliance with buyer specifications.

steps.heading: Production lots failing AQL final inspection

body.text: Production lots failing AQL final inspection are returned for 100% checking, defect correction, and re-inspection before packing authorization is re-sought.

steps.heading: Final inspection reports are completed for each production lot

body.text: Final inspection reports are completed for each production lot with results, AQL level applied, sample size, defects found by category, and pass/fail decision documented.

steps.heading: Pre-shipment inspection by buyer-nominated third-party inspection agencies

body.text: Pre-shipment inspection by buyer-nominated third-party inspection agencies is facilitated and coordinated by QA with all required documentation provided promptly.

sections.title: 10.4 Restricted Substances and Product Safety Compliance

body.text: All chemicals used in production including dyes, softeners, finishing agents, and adhesives are verified against buyer RSLs and applicable regulatory requirements before authorized use.

Supplier declarations and test certificates confirming RSL compliance are collected for all chemical inputs and maintained in the chemical compliance documentation system organized by chemical and supplier.
Finished garment laboratory testing for RSL compliance, color fastness, dimensional stability, and buyer-specified parameters is conducted by accredited test laboratories at defined frequencies.

steps.heading: Test reports are reviewed for compliance

body.text: Test reports are reviewed for compliance, filed in customer-specific documentation folders, and provided to buyers as evidence of product safety compliance on request.

steps.heading: All customer quality complaints are formally registered

body.text: All customer quality complaints are formally registered in the Customer Complaint Register with a unique reference number, date received, customer name, product details, and nature of complaint.

steps.heading: All complaints are acknowledged to the customer within 48 hours

body.text: All complaints are acknowledged to the customer within 48 hours of receipt. Formal responses including investigation findings and corrective actions are provided within agreed timelines.

steps.heading: Root cause analysis is conducted for all significant quality failures

body.text: Root cause analysis is conducted for all significant quality failures using structured methodology (5-Why, Fishbone Analysis) to identify true underlying causes.

steps.heading: Corrective and preventive actions addressing identified root causes

body.text: Corrective and preventive actions addressing identified root causes are documented in formal CAPA records with implementation owners, target completion dates, and effectiveness verification requirements.

steps.heading: Customer complaint data including frequency by type

body.text: Customer complaint data including frequency by type, product, buyer, and production line is analyzed monthly by QA management to identify systemic quality issues.

In-house quality testing equipment including measuring instruments, color light boxes, and other QC tools are calibrated at defined intervals by qualified technicians or external calibration services.
Calibration records including instrument ID, calibration date, results, and next due date are maintained and physically displayed on all calibrated instruments.

steps.heading: External accredited laboratory services are used

body.text: External accredited laboratory services are used for RSL testing and other specialized tests requiring analytical laboratory-grade capability.

blocks.text: All quality management activities comply with applicable buyer quality standards, international inspection standards (ASTM, AATCC, ISO), Bangladesh Export Policy requirements, and Bangladesh Standards and Testing Institution (BSTI) product standards where applicable. QMS documentation including inspection records, test reports, CAPA records, calibration certificates, and customer complaint files are maintained for minimum 3 years and are made available during buyer quality audits and third-party inspections.

The Company plans to strengthen its quality management system through implementation of a digital quality management platform for real-time defect tracking, trend analysis, and CAPA management. Future initiatives include introduction of Statistical Process Control (SPC) methods on high-volume production lines, expansion of in-house laboratory testing capability for basic RSL screening, development of a formal Quality Management System certified to ISO 9001 standards and launch of a Quality Ambassador program recognizing production workers who achieve exceptional quality performance.

narrative.text: Daily defect rate data by line and style is reviewed by QA supervisors and production management. Weekly quality performance summaries covering defect rates, rework volumes, AQL pass/fail rates, and customer complaint status are reviewed by the QA Manager. Monthly quality performance reports are presented to senior management covering trend analysis and corrective action status. Customer complaint closure rates and root cause recurrence rates are tracked as key quality performance indicators. The Quality Management SOP is reviewed annually.

sops.title: HUMAN RESOURCES MANAGEMENT, TALENT DEVELOPMENT & EMPLOYEE ENGAGEMENT

blocks.text: Padma Satel Arab Fashion Ltd. recognizes that its people are its most asset. The Company's HR Management SOP establishes systematic procedures for workforce planning, performance management, training and development, disciplinary management, and employee data management. These procedures ensure a productive, engaged, legally compliant, and well-managed workforce that contributes effectively to the Company's operational and sustainability objectives. All HR management practices are aligned with the Bangladesh Labour Act and international labor standards applicable to the RMG sector.

This SOP applies to all HR management activities covering recruitment, employment contracts, performance management, training and development, disciplinary procedures, and employee data management across all departments and organizational levels.

body.text: Annual workforce plans are prepared by HR in coordination with department heads covering planned headcount by department, skill requirements, anticipated turnover, and training needs for the coming operational year.
Succession planning for supervisory and management positions is reviewed annually by department heads and HR to identify high-potential workers for career development and advancement.
Internal promotion opportunities are actively prioritized to build internal talent pipelines and reward worker development before recruiting externally for supervisory and skilled positions.

All new employees undergo a comprehensive induction program before commencing independent work. Induction covers Company history and values, policies, Code of Conduct, safety rules, grievance procedure, worker rights, and job-specific work instructions.
Induction completion is formally documented with sign-off by both the employee confirming understanding and HR confirming completion of all required induction modules.
A formal probation period of typically 3 months is applied to new employees with performance reviewed at defined intervals and clear feedback provided.
Permanent appointment following successful probation completion is confirmed in writing and documented in the employee's personnel file.

Formal performance appraisals are conducted minimum annually for all permanent employees evaluating job performance against defined criteria, behavioral competencies, attendance, and development objectives.
Performance goals and expectations for the coming appraisal period are set and communicated clearly to employees at the beginning of each appraisal cycle.
Mid-year or quarterly informal performance check-in conversations between supervisors and workers are encouraged to provide timely feedback and support.
Appraisal outcomes are documented, signed by both appraiser and appraisee, linked to training and development plans, and used to inform promotion and salary review decisions.
Annual Training Needs Assessments are conducted for each department to identify skill gaps, compliance training requirements, and development opportunities for the coming year.

An Annual Training Calendar covering mandatory compliance training (safety, labor rights, environmental awareness, anti-corruption), technical skill development, and supervisory development is prepared and published.
Training effectiveness is evaluated through post-training assessments, supervisor observation of post-training performance, and periodic re-assessment of trained competencies.

Training records for every employee covering date, subject, trainer, duration, attendance, and assessment result are maintained in the Training Register and updated within 5 working days of each training event.

Disciplinary procedures are fair, transparent, and consistently applied following a progressive approach: verbal counseling, formal written warning, final written warning, and termination where warranted.

Workers are provided with clear information about the allegation or performance concern before any disciplinary decision is made. Workers have the right to respond and to be accompanied by a WPC representative if they choose.
All disciplinary proceedings, warnings issued, and dismissal decisions are documented with supporting evidence and signed by relevant parties, with records maintained in personnel files.
Disciplinary decisions are proportionate to the severity of the infraction. Summary dismissal is reserved for cases of gross misconduct as specifically defined in Company employment policy.

Comprehensive and accurate personnel files are maintained for all employees including employment contracts, personal information, qualification records, performance appraisals, training history, disciplinary records, and payroll records.
Employee records are stored securely with access restricted to authorized HR personnel and direct management on a strict need-to-know basis.

Employee personal data is collected, processed, and retained only for legitimate employment management purposes and is not shared with third parties without explicit authorization except as required by Bangladesh law.
Employees have the right to access and review their own personnel records upon formal written request to HR.

blocks.text: All HR management activities comply with the Bangladesh Labour Act, Bangladesh Labour Rules, Equal Remuneration Act, and other applicable employment legislation. HR records including employment contracts, payroll registers, training records, performance appraisals, disciplinary records, and termination documentation are maintained for minimum 5 years in compliance with legal retention requirements. The Company cooperates fully with labor regulatory inspections and buyer social compliance audits.

The Company plans to implement a digital HR management system to streamline employee records management, training tracking, performance appraisal processes, and payroll administration. Future HR development initiatives include launching a formal Leadership Development Program for supervisors and potential managers, introducing structured mentoring programs pairing experienced workers with new joiners, expanding the range of certified skills training programs available to production workers, and developing a formal Employee Well-being Program addressing physical, mental, and financial wellness.

narrative.text: HR performance indicators including headcount turnover rates, training completion rates by department, performance appraisal completion rates, disciplinary action frequency, and grievance resolution rates are reviewed monthly by the HR Manager. Quarterly HR performance reports are presented to senior management. Annual workforce reviews assess skills gaps, succession readiness, and training effectiveness. The HR Management SOP is reviewed annually.

sops.title: PRODUCTION OPERATIONS, PROCESS CONTROL & MANUFACTURING EXCELLENCE

blocks.text: Padma Satel Arab Fashion Ltd. operates multi-line garment manufacturing facilities producing a comprehensive range of woven, knit, and mixed fabrication apparel products for international buyers. Efficient, on-time, and quality-compliant production delivery is fundamental to the Company's commercial performance and customer relationships. This SOP establishes systematic procedures for production planning, cutting operations, sewing floor management, finishing, packing, inventory management, and lean manufacturing practices to ensure operational excellence across all production functions.

This SOP applies to all production-related activities including pre-production planning, cutting, sewing, finishing, packing, and dispatch, as well as production performance monitoring and operational improvement across all production floors and shifts.

body.text:
Production schedules are developed based on confirmed customer purchase orders, agreed delivery dates, current production capacity availability, material readiness status, and lead time requirements.
A Master Production Plan (MPP) is prepared for each order or production cycle communicating planned quantities, line allocations, production start and completion targets, and daily output targets to all relevant departments.
Daily production targets are set per line, communicated to supervisors at the start of each shift, and monitored against actual output throughout the shift with hourly tracking.
Production plan adherence is tracked daily. Deviations from plan exceeding defined thresholds trigger immediate review and corrective scheduling action.
Capacity planning reviews identify production bottlenecks, skill constraints, and machine availability limitations, and proactive corrective actions are planned.

Spreading plans and cutting lay plans are prepared by the cutting supervisor for each production lot to maximize fabric utilization efficiency and minimize waste.
Marker efficiency (fabric utilization percentage) is tracked for each cutting lot with improvement targets applied and continuously reviewed.
Fabric spreading is performed by trained spreaders following spreading standards covering fabric grain alignment, tension, ply counts, relaxation time, and shade consistency.
Cut panel quality checks covering notch accuracy, panel dimensions, fusing quality, and surface defects are conducted before panels are bundled and transferred to sewing lines.
Cutting records including lot number, fabric details, quantities cut, marker efficiency achieved, and panel inspection results are documented for each cutting lot.

Each sewing line operates under a designated line supervisor responsible for workflow management, quality monitoring, output tracking, worker performance guidance, and safety compliance.
Work-in-process (WIP) levels at each operation point are monitored to identify and resolve bottlenecks preventing balanced production flow across the line.
Preventive maintenance of all sewing machines is performed per documented maintenance schedules including daily operator-level care and periodic skilled maintenance.
Line balancing reviews are conducted when new styles are introduced or when significant output imbalances are observed, to optimize worker and operation time allocation.
Operator skill records identifying each operator's qualified operations are maintained and used to inform line assignments. Skill development programs are provided for operators requiring additional qualification.

All sewn garments pass through a systematic finishing process including thread trimming, measurement checking, pressing, fault rectification, and final appearance preparation.
Pressing and finishing quality parameters including temperature settings, steam pressure, and presentation standards are documented in work instructions for each garment style.
A finishing quality gate inspection is conducted by quality inspectors on all garments completing the finishing process before packing authorization.

Packing instructions for each order are prepared from buyer specifications covering polybag type and dimensions, folding method, garment size assortment, carton configuration, labeling, shipping marks, and special buyer requirements.
Packing supervisors verify that the packing team follows approved buyer-specific packing standards. QA inspections of packed cartons are conducted before palletization and dispatch clearance.
Dispatch documentation including packing lists, commercial invoices, bill of lading, export certificates, and shipping marks are prepared and verified against order requirements before shipment release.
Finished goods inventory is tracked from production completion through packing and shipment with accurate quantity records maintained at each stage.

5S methodology (Sort, Set in Order, Shine, Standardize, Sustain) is applied and maintained across all production and support areas. 5S audits are conducted periodically with results displayed on departmental visual management boards.
Production waste including fabric waste, defect and rework volumes, machine idle time, and transportation inefficiencies are measured monthly and targeted for progressive reduction.
Kaizen continuous improvement activities are encouraged through an active operator suggestion program. Accepted suggestions are implemented and the contributing worker recognized.
Time and motion studies are conducted for new product introductions to establish standard minute values and identify efficiency improvement opportunities.

blocks.text: All production operations comply with Bangladesh Export Policy requirements, applicable buyer production compliance standards, and the Company's internal quality management procedures. Production records including cut plans, inline inspection reports, final inspection reports, packing records, and dispatch documentation are maintained for minimum 3 years. The Company cooperates with buyer production monitoring visits and third-party factory assessments. Production activities related to environmental impact including fabric waste and energy consumption are managed in compliance with the Company's Environmental Management SOP.

The Company plans to invest in further automation of key production processes including automated fabric spreading and cutting technology to improve precision and reduce fabric waste. Future production improvement initiatives include implementation of a digital production monitoring system providing real-time floor output visibility, introduction of advanced line balancing software tools to optimize production flow, development of a formal Lean Manufacturing certification program for production supervisors, and expansion of the 5S program with quantified workplace organization targets linked to employee recognition.

narrative.text: Daily production output by line and style is reviewed by production management against plan. Weekly production performance summaries covering output achievement, efficiency rates, WIP levels, and machine downtime are reviewed by the Production Manager. Monthly production reports covering cumulative order progress, on-time delivery performance, and fabric waste percentages are presented to senior management. The Production Operations SOP is reviewed annually and updated to reflect operational improvements and technology changes.

sops.title: INFORMATION SECURITY, DATA PROTECTION & RECORDS MANAGEMENT

blocks.text: Padma Satel Arab Fashion Ltd. handles significant volumes of confidential information including customer order specifications, proprietary product designs, employee personal data, supplier commercial information, and financial records. Protecting the confidentiality, integrity, and availability of this information is essential to maintaining stakeholder trust, protecting competitive advantage, meeting contractual obligations, and complying with applicable data protection requirements. This SOP establishes systematic procedures for information classification, access control, data protection, incident response, recordkeeping, and third-party data confidentiality management.

This SOP applies to all information assets in any format - digital, paper, or verbal including customer data, production specifications, employee records, financial data, supplier information, and proprietary business information. It covers all employees, contractors, and authorized third parties with access to Company information.

rows.definition: Non-public information that could cause harm to the Company, customers, or workers if disclosed without authorization.
Unauthorized access, disclosure, loss, destruction, or alteration of confidential or personal information.
Technical and organizational measures restricting information access to authorized individuals based on their role and business need.
Any information relating to an identified or identifiable individual including employee records, contact details, and identification documents.

sections.title: 13.2 Customer Data and Intellectual Property Protection

blocks.text: All information security and data management activities comply with Bangladesh Information and Communication Technology Act, applicable contractual data protection obligations with international buyers, and the Company's internal records management policies. Employment contracts include confidentiality obligations for all workers with access to sensitive business or customer information. IT security controls, access rights records, incident reports, and records disposal documentation are maintained and reviewed regularly.

The Company plans to implement a formal Information Security Management System (ISMS) aligned with ISO 27001 principles to systematically manage information security risks across the organization. Future initiatives include deployment of multi-factor authentication for access to critical business systems, introduction of data loss prevention (DLP) software to prevent unauthorized data exfiltration, development of a formal Cybersecurity Incident Response Plan with clearly defined response procedures and escalation protocols, and annual cybersecurity awareness training for all staff.

narrative.text: IT system access rights are reviewed semi-annually by IT and HR. Security incident reports are reviewed monthly by IT management with trends presented to the Compliance Officer. Recordkeeping compliance is assessed during annual internal audits. Data backup success and recovery test results are reviewed monthly by IT. Third-party NDA status is reviewed quarterly by the Compliance function. The Information Security SOP is reviewed annually.

sops.title: SOCIAL COMPLIANCE, SUSTAINABILITY MANAGEMENT & INTERNATIONAL AUDIT READINESS

blocks.text: Padma Satel Arab Fashion Ltd. supplies garments to international buyers who require their manufacturing partners to maintain comprehensive compliance with social, environmental, and ethical standards as defined in international sustainability frameworks and buyer Codes of Conduct. The Company actively manages its sustainability assessment performance, social audit compliance, and buyer code of conduct adherence as strategic priorities. This SOP establishes systematic procedures for managing buyer compliance requirements, maintaining audit readiness across all social and sustainability programs, and driving continuous improvement across all sustainability themes: Environment, Labor & Human Rights, Ethics, and Sustainable Procurement.

This SOP applies to all activities supporting buyer compliance requirements, social audits, sustainability certifications, sustainability reporting, documentation management, and corrective action implementation across the Company.

body.text:
Applicable buyer codes of conduct and social compliance standards are obtained, reviewed, and communicated to relevant department heads and compliance personnel when new buyer relationships are established or existing codes are updated.
Gap assessments comparing current Company practices against buyer CoC requirements are conducted at minimum annually to identify areas requiring additional controls or documentation improvements.
Compliance improvements identified through gap assessments are tracked in a formal Corrective Action Register with defined owners, implementation timelines, and verification requirements.
Buyer-specific compliance requirements covering working hours, wages, safety, environmental requirements, and subcontractor management are incorporated into relevant departmental SOPs and work instructions.

A master document register covering all social audit-relevant records is maintained in organized, current, and immediately accessible format covering employment contracts, payroll records, working time records, training attendance, safety inspection records, environmental data, grievance records, and WPC minutes.
Internal self-assessment audits are conducted minimum annually against applicable standards including BSCI, SMETA, and WRAP to identify and proactively address non-conformances before external audit visits.
A dedicated audit coordination team comprising HR, Compliance, and relevant department heads is designated to manage all audit logistics, documentation preparation, auditor interaction, and worker interview facilitation.
Audit findings and Corrective Action Plans are developed with prioritized, time-bound actions assigned to specific department owners. Follow-up evidence is documented and provided to auditors within agreed timelines.
Audit results including scores, findings, and CAP status are reviewed in management review meetings and incorporated into continuous improvement planning.

The Company actively participates in third-party sustainability assessments as required by buyers and certification bodies covering environmental management, labor & human rights, ethics, and sustainable procurement themes.
A dedicated sustainability evidence folder is maintained in digital format organized by assessment question category, containing current and verified supporting documents for all applicable sustainability indicators.
Annual sustainability self-assessment responses are prepared with comprehensive supporting evidence covering energy management policies and consumption data, GHG emission monitoring, waste management programs, water management, labor practices, anti-corruption measures, and supply chain management.
Sustainability assessment scores, scorecard feedback, and improvement recommendations are reviewed by management within 30 days of receipt. Specific improvement actions are developed and incorporated into the annual sustainability improvement plan.
Continuous improvement in sustainability performance is a stated organizational objective with specific improvement targets reviewed annually. Responsibility for each improvement area is formally assigned to the relevant department head.

A Certification Register is maintained listing all applicable certifications with certification body details, current certificate number, validity period, renewal due date, and responsible owner for renewal management.
Certification renewal activities including document preparation, audit scheduling, and fee management are initiated minimum 3 months before certificate expiry to prevent any lapse in certification status.
Current certificates are displayed in the factory, and copies are provided to customers and auditors upon request.
Certification requirements are communicated to relevant departments and incorporated into operational procedures and training programs.

Annual sustainability performance data covering energy consumption, GHG emissions, water consumption, waste generation and recycling rates, labor indicators, and social audit results is compiled by the Compliance/Sustainability function.
Sustainability performance data is disclosed to customers, certification bodies, and sustainability rating organizations as required by commercial agreements and assessment timelines.
The Company maintains transparency in sustainability reporting and does not make misleading or unsubstantiated claims regarding its environmental or social performance.

blocks.text: All social compliance and sustainability management activities comply with applicable Bangladesh labor laws and environmental regulations, ILO Core Conventions applicable to Bangladesh, and the requirements of buyer Codes of Conduct including BSCI, SMETA, WRAP, and applicable textile sector sustainability standards. Social audit compliance documentation, certification records, sustainability data, and corrective action plans are maintained for minimum 5 years and made available during buyer and third-party audits.

The Company plans to develop a formal Corporate Sustainability Report to comprehensively communicate environmental, social, and governance performance to customers, investors, and other stakeholders. Future sustainability initiatives include implementing the HIGG Facility Environmental Module (FEM) and Facility Social & Labor Module (FSLM) as standardized sustainability performance measurement tools, developing a formal Science-Based Target for GHG emission reduction aligned with recognized climate science, expanding the scope of supply chain sustainability assessments to cover more Tier 2 suppliers, and establishing a formal Sustainability Committee at management level to govern the Company's sustainability strategy.

narrative.text: Sustainability compliance performance indicators including active certification validity status, social audit CAP closure rates, sustainability assessment scores, and buyer compliance assessment outcomes are reviewed quarterly by the Compliance/Sustainability function and reported to senior management. Annual sustainability performance reviews set improvement targets across all sustainability dimensions for the coming year. The Social Compliance and Sustainability Management SOP is reviewed annually.
